source_note: Official DORA text (OJ L 333, 27.12.2022), retrieved from the EU Publications Office. All 64 article numbers and titles taken from it.
note: Applies only to EU financial entities listed in Art. 2 (banks, payment and e-money institutions, investment firms, insurers, crypto-asset service providers, etc.) and to critical ICT third-party service providers serving them.

articles.name: Governance and organisation
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Management body defines, approves and is accountable for the ICT risk management framework (5(2)).

articles.name: ICT risk management framework
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Documented framework; strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools; annual review and internal audit.

articles.name: ICT systems, protocols and tools
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management.

articles.name: Identification
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Identify and classify ICT-supported business functions, information assets and dependencies, including third parties.

articles.name: Protection and prevention
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Continuous monitoring and control of ICT systems; least privilege, strong authentication, patching, change management (9(4)).

articles.name: Detection
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities and ICT network performance issues.

articles.name: Response and recovery
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. ICT business continuity policy, response and recovery plans; tested; crisis communication.

articles.name: Backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Backups, segregated restoration, recovery time and recovery point objectives.

articles.name: Learning and evolving
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Post-incident reviews and lessons learned; ICT security awareness training.

articles.name: Communication
articles.description: Chapter II — ICT risk management. Crisis communication plans for clients, counterparts and the public.

articles.name: ICT-related incident management process
articles.description: Chapter III — ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting. Process to detect, manage, record and notify ICT-related incidents; root-cause analysis.

articles.name: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
articles.description: Chapter III — ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting. Classify by clients affected, duration, geographical spread, data losses, criticality of services and economic impact.

articles.name: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
articles.description: Chapter III — ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting. Report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority: initial notification, intermediate report and final report (19(4)); inform clients (19(3)).

articles.name: General requirements for the performance of digital operational resilience testing
articles.description: Chapter IV — Digital operational resilience testing. Sound, comprehensive testing programme, performed by independent parties, at least yearly on critical systems.

articles.name: Testing of ICT tools and systems
articles.description: Chapter IV — Digital operational resilience testing. Vulnerability assessments, scans, scenario-based, compatibility, performance and end-to-end testing, penetration testing.

articles.name: Advanced testing of ICT tools, systems and processes based on TLPT
articles.description: Chapter IV — Digital operational resilience testing. Threat-led penetration testing at least every 3 years for entities identified by the authority.

articles.name: Requirements for testers for the carrying out of TLPT
articles.description: Chapter IV — Digital operational resilience testing.

articles.name: General principles
articles.description: Chapter V, Section I — Key principles for a sound management of ICT third-party risk. Entity remains fully responsible; ICT third-party risk strategy; register of information on all contractual arrangements; exit strategies.

articles.name: Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk at entity level
articles.description: Chapter V, Section I — Key principles for a sound management of ICT third-party risk. Assess ICT concentration risk and sub-outsourcing before contracting.

articles.name: Key contractual provisions
articles.description: Chapter V, Section I — Key principles for a sound management of ICT third-party risk. Mandatory contract terms: service description, locations, availability and integrity, audit and access rights, termination, exit.
